sonnet.problem: The True statement mostly repeats the story card right before it. Card 3 already says Paul tells wives to submit to their husbands, so the only new part is 'as to the Lord'.
sonnet.rule: A True statement never just repeats the card before it.

sonnet.problem: The question says Paul calls the line about a man and his wife becoming one flesh a profound mystery. Verse 32 only says 'This mystery is profound' and never says what 'this mystery' points back to, so the card ties the two together when the text leaves it open.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: Two wrong answers mean nearly the same thing: 'customs and ways of their ancestors' and 'wisdom and traditions of the elders'. The right answer is also the only one that mentions the Lord, so it stands out.
sonnet.rule: Two wrong answers never mean the same as each other either.

sonnet.problem: This story card comes after card 11 asked about verse 6. It retells that same fact ('Not just while someone's watching, but as servants of Christ') and reads like a reaction to the baker's pick.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.
